claim: Apple is the source of truth for installs (67 lifetime iOS first-time downloads). RevenueCat opens a customer per SDK init and roughly DOUBLES that, so never use it as an install denominator.

body.what: tools/autonomous/appstore_downloads.py reads App Downloads Standard (r3) and App Store Purchases Standard (r12) from the App Store Connect analytics request into nightly CSV series at /opt/dale/data/treesmith-appstore-downloads.csv and treesmith-appstore-purchases.csv, the way appstore_sources.py already reads discovery (r14). Apple's own install and purchase counts, previously unread.
body.verified_against: Reproduced DEC-321's hand pull EXACTLY from the frozen ONE_TIME_SNAPSHOT request: 51 first-time downloads, 4 redownloads, AU 22 / US 17; and 3 purchases, US$77.30 sales, US$52.37 proceeds, AU 1 / PK 1 / US 1. That match is the evidence the reader is right rather than merely plausible.
body.held_now: 75 days, 2026-04-30 to 2026-09-14. 67 lifetime first-time downloads, 4 redownloads, 2 restores, 149 updates. First-time by territory AU 29, US 22, then a long single-digit tail. By source: App Store search 42, App referrer 13, Web referrer 6, App Store browse 3, Unavailable 3.
body.rate: 0.45 first-time downloads/day over the 113 pre-gap days (51/113); 1.78/day over the 9 observed days 2026-09-06..09-14 (16 downloads). ~4x, but CONFOUNDED and not a verdict: the rename and the 1.0.11 release (2026-09-13) both land inside that window and its two biggest days (5 and 4) ARE the release days. n=9 days.
body.r3_window_is_2_days_not_3: MEASURED across all 9 live instances: each r3 DAILY instance carries exactly [processing_date-2, processing_date-1]. Narrower than r14's 3-day window (DEC-332), so the downloads series is MORE fragile to a missed pull than discovery is. pull_gaps() detects unobserved stretches from pulled_at spacing against that width and the render names them.
body.r12_has_no_ongoing_instances: SUPERSEDED BY DEC-339 / DAL-300 (2026-09-17). r12 is NOT broken and was never ungranted. Apple emits an instance only for a report with events in the window, and we have had ZERO App Store purchases since the ongoing request began 2026-09-06 (RevenueCat: newest production sale 2026-08-23; 28d overview US$24 gross, MRR 0, active subs 0). The control was inside the same request: r10/r11 Pre-Orders and r224-r227 Subscription reports also have 0 instances on BOTH requests, and those are products we have never sold. r12 has 1 instance on the SNAPSHOT, whose span contained 3 purchases. Every empty report is a product with no events. Do NOT re-open this as a broken-report ticket.
body.lost_span: 2026-08-21 to 2026-09-05 is UNOBTAINABLE for downloads, the same handover hole that cost discovery 2026-08-21..09-04 (DEC-332). The render prints it as a PULL GAP rather than averaging over it. 47 other days carry no row and ARE real zeroes: at ~1 download a day a quiet day is ordinary, so no_row_days and pull_gaps are deliberately different concepts.
body.revenuecat_inflation_reconfirmed: Apple: 67 lifetime iOS first-time downloads. RevenueCat: ~134 iOS customer records. RevenueCat opens a customer per SDK init, so it roughly DOUBLES the install count. Apple is the source of truth for installs; RevenueCat stays the source of truth for money.
body.guards: tests/test_appstore_downloads.py, 20 tests. Per DEC-326 the two rules that matter were each proven to FAIL before being trusted: reverting the instance merge to summing breaks the overlapping-day test (6 != 3), and disabling the NotReady guard breaks the no-instances test.
